`{migraph}` helps new users install and learn social network analysis in R.
One install gives you the full set of stocnet packages
for making, manipulating, plotting, measuring, testing, and modelling networks,
and a set of interactive tutorials that teach you how to use them.
All the functions work with base R matrices and edgelists,
and with [`{igraph}`](https://igraph.org/r/),
[`{network}`](https://statnet.org), and
[`{tidygraph}`](https://tidygraph.data-imaginist.com/index.html) objects,
for one-mode and two-mode (bipartite) networks.

## Install

Install `{migraph}` from CRAN.
Open the R console and type:

```r
install.packages("migraph")
```

Then load it:

```r
library(migraph)
```

This also loads [`{manynet}`](https://stocnet.github.io/manynet/),
[`{autograph}`](https://stocnet.github.io/autograph/),
[`{netrics}`](https://stocnet.github.io/netrics/), and
[`{infernet}`](https://stocnet.github.io/infernet/),
so you have all their functions and data at once.

Some functions and tutorials use other packages for one or two specific tasks.
`{migraph}` asks to install these when you first need them.
To install them all now, type:

```r
install.packages("migraph", dependencies = TRUE)
```

## Stay current

The stocnet packages change frequently, with fixes and new features.
When you load `{migraph}`, it tells you if a newer version of one of these packages is available
(it checks at most once a week).
To check now and install all the newest versions, type:

```r
update_stocnet()
```

Do this before a class, a test, or the submission of a paper.
For each package, `update_stocnet()` installs the newer of the CRAN release 
and the GitHub release.

## Learn

`{migraph}` gives you interactive `{learnr}` tutorials from all the stocnet packages.
Type `run_tute()` to see the list, and `run_tute("manynet1")` (for example) to start one.
`extract_tute()` saves the code of a tutorial as an R script.
We suggest that you do the tutorials in this sequence:

```{r tutorials, echo = FALSE}
pkgs <- c("migraph", "manynet", "autograph", "netrics", "infernet")
tutes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pkgs, function(p)
  as.data.frame(learnr::available_tutorials(p))[, c("package", "name", "title")]))
# The introduction to R comes first, then the packages in the sequence of the
# analysis.
first <- tutes$name == "tutorial0"
rank <- ifelse(first, 0, match(tutes$package, c(pkgs[-1], "migraph")))
tutes <- tutes[order(rank, tutes$name), ]
knitr::kable(tutes, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("Package", "Name", "Title"))
```

## The packages

| Package | What it does | For example |
|---|---|---|
| [`{manynet}`](https://stocnet.github.io/manynet/) | makes, imports, coerces, and manipulates network data | `as_igraph()`, `to_undirected()`, `generate_random()` |
| [`{autograph}`](https://stocnet.github.io/autograph/) | plots networks and the results of analyses | `graphr()`, `plot()` |
| [`{netrics}`](https://stocnet.github.io/netrics/) | measures and marks nodes, ties, and networks | `node_by_degree()`, `net_by_density()` |
| [`{infernet}`](https://stocnet.github.io/infernet/) | tests and models networks: CUG and QAP tests, MRQAP, and diffusions | `test_random()`, `estimate_mrqap()`, `play_diffusions()` |
| `{migraph}` | loads and updates all of these, and holds the tutorials and the data of the book | `run_tute()`, `update_stocnet()` |

## Data

<img style="border:10px solid white;" src="https://jameshollway.com/media/9781108833509pvs01.jpg" align="left" alt="Cover image of the book Multimodal Political Networks" width="125"/>

`{migraph}` is the software companion to the book:

> David Knoke, Mario Diani, James Hollway, and Dimitris Christopoulos (2021) [*Multimodal Political Networks*](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/multimodal-political-networks/43EE8C192A1B0DCD65B4D9B9A7842128).
Cambridge University Press: Cambridge.

It includes most of the datasets in the book:
`r list_data("mpn_")`.
The stocnet packages together implement most of the methods in the book.

<br clear="left"/>

## Funding details

Most work on this package has been funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)
[Grant Number 188976](https://data.snf.ch/grants/grant/188976): 
"Power and Networks and the Rate of Change in Institutional Complexes" (PANARCHIC).
